issues.description: Compiled script content is shipped through the compile RPC payload instead of a dedicated download/read endpoint.
issues.detail: All six reviewers flag this as wrong shape: the backend already writes the file and returns its path, yet stuffs full script content into every compile_notebook response. This bloats memory and bandwidth, has no size bound, and complects 'where the artifact lives' with 'what it contains'. Add a separate download/read-script RPC keyed by path, fetched on click.

issues.description: open() lacks explicit encoding and post-success error handling.
issues.detail: open(script_path) relies on platform default encoding, leaking locale behavior through the RPC contract. Any IOError after successful compilation propagates as a compile_notebook failure, conflating two concerns. Specify encoding='utf-8' and either handle the read error separately or move the read to a dedicated endpoint with stated preconditions.

issues.description: Full script content threaded through multiple React state/prop layers when a path-on-click fetch would suffice.
issues.detail: compiledContent flows through DeployProgressState, DeploysProgress, DeployProgress, and Commands purely to feed a Blob at click time. This is prop-drilling arbitrary-size file bodies through a UI progress widget. Fetch from backend by path on click instead, eliminating duplicated path/content state.

issues.description: Download button rendered unconditionally while handler guards on compiledContent, producing silent no-op clicks.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick checks props.compiledPath && props.compiledContent and returns silently on failure, but the icon renders unconditionally in the success branch. Either the guard is dead code or the rendering invariant is wrong. Gate icon rendering on compiledContent or make the field a precondition of the success-branch type.

issues.description: GetAppIcon used as a click target instead of a real button; no keyboard or accessibility affordance.
issues.detail: An SVG icon with onClick has no role, no keyboard handler, and no focus ring. The adjacent 'Done' anchor is a proper element for a reason. Wrap in <button>/IconButton or use <a download> with an object URL to match the surrounding code's voice and be keyboard reachable.

issues.description: Filename derivation via split('/').pop() with fabricated fallback is fragile and platform-dependent.
issues.detail: split('/').pop() returns the full path on Windows-hosted notebook servers and an empty string when the path ends in a slash, triggering the 'pipeline.kale.py' fallback that contradicts the actual artifact name. Use a proper path basename utility and state the path-shape invariant at the server boundary.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches strong consensus: the feature works but picked the wrong data shape. All six reviewers flag that stuffing the entire compiled script into every compile_notebook RPC response, then threading it through multiple React state layers to re-blob on click, is bloat where a path-based download endpoint would compose cleanly with the browser's native download. The Python read lacks explicit encoding and error separation. On the frontend, the download icon renders unconditionally while the handler guards silently, the icon is not a real button, and filename derivation is fragile. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — refactor to a dedicated download RPC fetched on click, fix encoding and accessibility, and remove duplicated state.
